setup: Lie on your side, bottom knee bent
Top leg straight, in line with your body
Hips stacked, hand on the top hip
execution: Lift the top leg up and slightly back
Lead with the heel, toes forward
Pause at the top, then lower slowly
Keep the hip from rolling back
faults: Don't turn the toes up to the ceiling
Don't hitch your waist to lift higher

notes: The range is small; lift only as high as you can with the hips still stacked.
An ankle weight or band adds load later. Ankle weights have no equipment kind yet, so this entry logs no load.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain at the front or side of the hip
Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Camera looking at the front of the figure lying on its side, head to the left, so the top leg's lift and the stacked hips are clear.

keyPositions.label: Down
keyPositions.describe: Lying on the side, head on the bottom arm, bottom knee bent for balance. Top leg straight, in line with the trunk, resting on the bottom leg. Top hand on the hip.

keyPositions.label: Up
keyPositions.describe: Top leg lifted to about 35–40°, slightly behind the body line, heel leading and toes facing forward. Hips still stacked.

ikHints: Pelvis stays stacked; trunk does not move
emphasise: Leg lifts slightly behind the body line

sources.title: Brookbush Institute summary of DiStefano et al. (2009) gluteal activation in 12 exercises, J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 39(7):532-40

sources.note: Secondary summary of an EMG study (21 recreationally active adults). EMG activity is not growth or strength.
